baseplate.name: Baseplate
baseplate.does: The steel frame the pump and its motor are bolted to, grouted to the floor, so that their shafts stay in line.

volute.name: Casing (volute)
volute.does: Takes the water in at the suction nozzle to the impeller's eye and gathers it from the impeller's tips in a passage that grows round the casing to the discharge nozzle. It stays on its pipes when the pump is opened.

frame.name: Bearing frame (power end)
frame.does: Holds the shaft in its two bearings and the oil that lubricates them; with the casing cover, the shaft, the seal and the impeller it is the back pull-out assembly, drawn out of the casing without disturbing the pipes.

casing_cover.name: Casing cover (seal chamber)
casing_cover.does: Closes the casing behind the impeller; the mechanical seal sits in its bore round the shaft.

impeller.name: Impeller
impeller.does: A closed impeller: its six vanes, curved back against the way it turns, fling the water outwards from the eye into the volute. Screwed or keyed onto the shaft's end.
impeller.material: Cast iron, bronze or stainless steel

shaft.name: Shaft
shaft.does: Carries the impeller at one end and the coupling hub at the other, turning in the frame's bearings.

seal.name: Mechanical seal
seal.does: Stops the pumped water leaking along the shaft: a rotating face on the shaft runs against a stationary seat in the cover's gland.
seal.material: Carbon and silicon carbide faces, elastomer and stainless steel parts

bearing_ib.name: Inboard bearing
bearing_ib.does: The bearing nearer the impeller: carries the radial load.

bearing_ob.name: Outboard (thrust) bearing
bearing_ob.does: The bearing at the coupling end: carries the radial and the axial thrust.

end_cover.name: Bearing end cover
end_cover.does: Closes the frame at the coupling end round the shaft, holding the outboard bearing in place and the oil in.

coupling.name: Spacer coupling
coupling.does: Joins the pump's shaft to the motor's; its spacer lets the back pull-out assembly come out without moving the motor. Drawn here as one piece with its hubs.
coupling.material: Steel hubs and spacer, flexible elements

guard.name: Coupling guard
guard.does: Covers the turning coupling; the pump never runs without it.

motor.name: Motor: stator and frame
motor.does: The finned frame with its feet holds the stator core and its three-phase winding; the rotating field the winding makes turns the rotor. Cooled from outside by the fan's air over the fins (IC 411).
motor.material: Cast iron frame, laminated electrical steel core, copper winding

terminal_box.name: Terminal box
terminal_box.does: Where the supply cable lands on the winding's terminals U1, V1, W1; record the connections before it is opened.

end_shield_de.name: Drive-end shield
end_shield_de.does: Closes the frame at the drive end and holds the drive-end bearing in its housing; its bearing cap keeps the grease in.

end_shield_nde.name: Non-drive-end shield
end_shield_nde.does: Closes the frame at the fan end and holds the non-drive-end bearing in its housing.

fan.name: Cooling fan
fan.does: On the shaft's non-drive end: blows air along the frame's fins whichever way the motor turns (straight radial blades). A fan fitted with interference is replaced, not reused.

fan_cowl.name: Fan cowl
fan_cowl.does: Guards the fan and guides its air over the fins.
fan_cowl.sealed_why: The grille is part of the fan cowl: they come off as one.

grille.name: Air intake grille
grille.does: Lets the cooling air in at the cowl's end; kept clear of dirt.

rotor.name: Rotor
rotor.does: The squirrel-cage rotor on its shaft: the stator's field drives it round. Drawn out of the stator's bore without touching the winding.
rotor.material: Laminated steel core, aluminium cage, steel shaft

bearing_de.name: Drive-end bearing
bearing_de.does: A rolling bearing on the shaft at the drive end, in the drive-end shield: it carries the load the coupling puts on the shaft.

bearing_nde.name: Non-drive-end bearing
bearing_nde.does: A rolling bearing on the shaft at the fan end, in the non-drive-end shield.

text: The baseplate stays grouted to the floor.
The casing stays bolted to the baseplate and to its suction and discharge pipes.
why: The back pull-out design lets the rest come out without disturbing the pipes.

text: The motor stands on the baseplate, on its shims.
why: The spacer coupling lets the back pull-out assembly come out without moving the motor; its own parts come apart as the motor kind's do.

text: Slide the rotor, its bearings already on its shaft, into the stator's bore from the drive end, its weight carried so that it never rests on the winding.
why: A rotor dragged against the winding damages its insulation. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: motor
The rotor goes into the stator's bore: set the stator down first.
Draw the rotor out before the stator is moved.

text: The drive-end bearing is fitted on the shaft before the rotor goes in: heated, pressed on its inner ring only.
why: It comes off the shaft once the rotor is out. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: The non-drive-end bearing is fitted on the shaft the same way, before the rotor goes in.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Fit the non-drive-end shield over its bearing and into the frame, with its bearing cap.
why: Its spigot is entered square, without forcing, so that the bearing is not loaded. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: bearing_nde
The shield's housing closes over the non-drive-end bearing: fit the bearing first.
Take the non-drive-end shield off before its bearing.

text: Fit the drive-end shield over its bearing and into the frame, with its bearing cap.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: bearing_de
The shield's housing closes over the drive-end bearing: fit the bearing first.
Take the drive-end shield off before its bearing.
rotor
The drive-end shield closes the stator over the rotor: put the rotor in first.
Take the drive-end shield off before the rotor is drawn out.

text: Fit the four drive-end shield bolts and tighten them evenly; turn the shaft by hand: it must turn freely.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: end_shield_de
The bolts hold the drive-end shield: fit the shield first.
Take the four bolts out before the drive-end shield comes off.

text: Push the fan onto the shaft's non-drive end and lock it.
why: A fan fitted with interference is pulled with a puller, never knocked off, and replaced. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: end_shield_nde
The fan sits behind the non-drive-end shield: fit the shield first.
Pull the fan off before the non-drive-end shield comes off.

text: Put the fan cowl over the fan.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: fan
The cowl closes over the fan: fit the fan first.
Take the fan cowl off before the fan.

text: The grille comes with the fan cowl.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Fit the four cowl screws.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: fan_cowl
The screws hold the cowl: put the cowl on first.
Take the four cowl screws out before the cowl comes off.

text: Fit the terminal box and connect the supply as recorded before it was opened.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: motor
The terminal box sits on the stator's frame: set the stator down first.
Take the terminal box off before the stator is moved.

text: Set the bearing frame on the bench.
Slide the shaft, its bearings already on it, into the frame from the coupling end.
needs: frame
The shaft goes into the bearing frame: set the frame down first.
Draw the shaft out of the frame before the frame is moved.

text: The inboard bearing is fitted on the shaft on the bench, before the shaft goes into the frame: heated, pressed on its inner race only.
why: It comes off the shaft once the shaft is out of the frame; bearings are never reused once removed.

text: The outboard bearing is fitted on the shaft the same way, with its locknut, before the shaft goes into the frame.
Fit the bearing end cover at the coupling end.
needs: bearing_ob
The end cover holds the outboard bearing: fit the bearing first.
Take the end cover off before the shaft and its bearings are drawn out.
shaft
The end cover closes the frame round the shaft: put the shaft in first.
Take the end cover off before the shaft is drawn out.

text: Slide the mechanical seal onto the shaft, its faces clean.
needs: shaft
The seal goes on the shaft: put the shaft in first.
Take the seal off the shaft before the shaft is drawn out of the frame.

text: Fit the casing cover over the seal to the frame.
needs: seal
The cover closes over the seal: fit the seal first.
Take the casing cover off before the seal.

text: Screw the impeller onto the shaft's end, holding the shaft with a shaft wrench.
why: It unscrews counter-clockwise seen from the impeller end.
needs: casing_cover
The impeller goes on in front of the casing cover: fit the cover first.
Take the impeller off before the casing cover.
shaft
The impeller goes on the shaft: put the shaft in first.
Take the impeller off before the shaft is drawn out.

text: Slide the back pull-out assembly into the casing with a new gasket and tighten the twelve casing bolts evenly.
needs: frame
The bolts hold the back pull-out assembly to the casing: put it in first.
Take the casing bolts out before the back pull-out assembly is pulled.
casing_cover
The bolts clamp the casing cover: fit the cover first.
Take the casing bolts out before the casing cover comes off.
impeller
The impeller goes on before the back pull-out assembly goes into the casing.
Pull the back pull-out assembly before the impeller comes off.

text: Fit the coupling's spacer between the hubs and check the alignment.
needs: motor
The coupling joins the pump to the motor: set the motor down first.
Take the coupling out before the motor is lifted.
rotor
The coupling's motor hub sits on the motor's shaft: put the rotor in first.
Take the coupling out before the motor's rotor is drawn out.
casing_bolts
The coupling joins the pump's shaft to the motor's: bolt the back pull-out assembly in first.
Take the coupling out before the back pull-out assembly is pulled.

text: Fit the coupling guard.
why: The pump never runs without its coupling guard.
needs: coupling
The guard covers the coupling: fit the coupling first.
Take the coupling guard off first.
